Maya (CSM): Heads up — I'm drafting a customer-facing one-pager runbook for onboarding/renewal checks focusing on caching/batching/streaming. Short + actionable. Putting draft below. @Sam (Eng) @Jordan (ML) pls flag any inaccuracies.

Sam (Eng): Looks good. Quick q — do we call out SDK flags vs server defaults? I think both.

Maya (CSM): Yep both. I added 'recommended' and 'strict' sections. Also added emergency fallback policy.

Jordan (ML): Suggest adding note about KV-cache warmup for multi-turn chat. If you expect long sessions, prefill KV with the first N tokens during warmup window.

Alex (Solutions): For customers on Dedicated, include autoscale trigger example: `cpu > 75% for 2m` and burst policy note. Also include guidance on quantized model compatibility.

Maya (CSM): Draft runbook pasted below.

cs-bot: File uploaded: runbook-one-pager-draft.pdf :page_facing_up:

Maya (CSM): RUNBOOK DRAFT — CUSTOMER-FACING ONE-PAGER
- Goal: keep initial response latency <= 300ms p50 and prevent token-cost surprises.
- When to use:
  • Use prefix caching for stable system prompts
  • Use client-side batching for high-concurrency bursts
  • Use streaming for first-token-sensitive UX

Quick steps for customers:
1) Prefill and static prompt caching
   - Cache system prompt + few history messages.
   - TTL: 24h for static system prompts; shorter for user-specific state.
   - Example SDK snippet:
```:
client.config.cache.set('system_prompt_v1', prompt, ttl=86400)
``` 
2) Batching guidance
   - Use small batches (4-16) for low-latency workloads; larger (32-128) for throughput.
   - Set max_wait_ms to 20-50ms to avoid holding single requests too long.
   - Example:
```:
batcher = Batcher(max_batch_size=16, max_wait_ms=30)
``` 
3) Streaming best-practices
   - Use streaming for token-by-token UX and optimistic rendering.
   - Add a client-side 200ms "skeleton" before stream data to hint progress for slow networks.

Escalation & health checks:
- If p50 > 500ms: check cache hit rate (>70% ideal) and batch queue length.
- If error spikes: check model fallback logs and rate-limit headers.
- Contact flow: first DM Maya (CSM) -> escalate to Sam (Eng) -> open infra ticket if needed.

Emergency fallback policy (recommended):
1) For timeouts > 3s, fallback to cached response or condensed model:
   - Prefer: cached summary for identical prompts
   - Alternative: route to 'fast-quant' model and mark flagged for eval.
2) Example policy rule (pseudo):
```:
if latency > 3000ms:
  route -> model:fast-quant-v1
  tag -> 'fallback:timeout'
```

Monitoring checklist to share with customer:
- Expose cache_hit_rate, batch_queue_len, mean_latency, error_rate
- Set alert: cache_hit_rate drop of >20% in 10m
- Monthly review: sample prompts + qualitative QA

TL;DR: Cache stable bits, batch conservatively, stream for UX, fallback to cached/quantized variant on severe delays.

Sam (Eng): I added a tiny nit: change max_wait_ms to 25 in example — reduces average tail latency.

Maya (CSM): Good catch. Updated.

Kevin (Support): Can we add a one-liner for self-serve customers about toggling 'prefill_on_startup' in Console? Saves a bunch of tickets.

Maya (CSM): Added. Final ask: Alex, can you make a PDF + one-slide summary for next week's customer workshop?

Alex (Solutions): On it. I'll share by EOD.

Maya (CSM): Thanks all :heart: — will publish to the shared playbooks page after review.
